prompt:
Extract a SysML v2 model from the document as a list of facts. Each fact has unit_id (the sentence it comes from), type and slots. Give only the slots that have a value, as a list of {slot, value} pairs; for composition give one 'parts' pair per part.

Types and slots:
  attribute(owner,name,value,unit) action(performer,label) state(owner,label) constraint(subject,expression) requirement(subject,text)
  composition(whole,parts) flow(source,target,payload) succession(before,after) transition(from,to,trigger) allocation(action,to)

Name each element by its full name as first introduced in the document.
RULES:
- Resolve every entity-valued slot using all the text you are given. If a sentence refers to an element by an alias, abbreviation, pronoun or shorter description, write the element's full name as first introduced. If a sentence says an element receives or uses an item and the text you are given states which element produces or sends that item, emit a flow from that producer to the receiver. If an element cannot be determined from the text you are given, use null; never guess.
- Never write placeholder words such as "any", "all", "some state" for an unstated element; use null.
- Do not merge differently named things unless the text says they are the same.
- Emit one action for EVERY behavior verb phrase, including passive voice (performer null), capability statements, displays, logs, generates and reports. label = the verbatim verb phrase with its object.
- Emit a requirement for every NORMATIVE statement (shall, must, should, will, is required to, needs to). Purpose, goal or benefit sentences are not requirements.
- Emit a state for every named mode or state; transitions use the state names, with from null when the prior state is not stated.
- Emit a succession only for an EXPLICIT temporal connective between two actions ("then", "after", "once", "before", "when ... is complete", "next", "finally"); before/after are the action labels. Never use succession for cause or data transfer.
- Resolve a pronoun or "this/these" performer to the element named in the preceding sentence and write that element's name; if it cannot be resolved, use null. Never output a pronoun as a slot value.
- Drop determiners and quantifiers from element names ("Each Soil Moisture Probe" -> "Soil Moisture Probe", "the system" -> "system").
- allocation.to must be a component or actor, never a mode or state.
- Emit a constraint for every threshold, limit, period or deadline stated with a number; expression = the verbatim phrase.
- Emit a flow for every sentence in which an element sends, transmits, reports, displays, commands or delivers an item (target null if the receiver is not named).
 Also list under "entities" every system element, actor or item named in the document units, with its full name and any alias the text explicitly declares for it (e.g. 'hereafter X', 'known as X', 'called X'); aliases [] if none. Return JSON {"entities": [...], "facts": [...]}.

Memory from EARLIER parts of the document (do not extract facts from it; use it only to resolve names, aliases and who produces an item):
Warehouse system boundary: from receiving interface to release of completed outbound load at shipping interface; pallets stay inside while inspected, identified, buffered, stored, retrieved, prepared for dispatch. Elements: Inbound Inspection Desk (records inspection outcomes before accepted pallets enter storage); Pallet Dimension Scanner (captures dimensions for handling/storage eligibility); Inbound Pallet Buffer (temporarily holds accepted pallets when storage can't proceed); North Aisle Stacker Crane and South Aisle Stacker Crane (storage/retrieval in designated aisles); East Transfer Conveyor and West Transfer Conveyor (carry pallets on transfer routes); Conveyor Line Controller (coordinates conveyor movement); Autonomous Forklift Fleet (moves pallets only in approved areas under authorized tasking); Yard Gate Controller (vehicle access at perimeter); Outbound Dispatch Sorter (sequences eligible pallets for dispatch); Outbound Checkweigh Scale (verifies pallet weight before shipment completion); Shipping Documentation Desk (prepares outbound load records); Safety Zone Controller (enforces movement restrictions in protected areas); Fire Alarm Panel (provides facility alarm status); Maintenance Release Terminal (records equipment availability for planning). Actor: Warehouse Operations Supervisor (exceptions, priorities, recovery decisions). Warehouse Management System, alias Morrowglass: authority for inventory records and work release; maintains authoritative status, location, handling eligibility of each pallet. Requirements: inbound acceptance requires valid receipt instruction and safely handleable pallet; inbound arrivals checked against scheduled delivery window before door assignment; storage locations assigned for safe handling, efficient retrieval, inventory controls; no equipment may start inventory-moving work without authorized release from Warehouse Management System; physical movement and system inventory status must be reconciled; objective: process accepted pallets accurately, meet committed dispatch times without bypassing safety or inventory controls.

Document units:
S028: The Yard Gate Controller records vehicle identity, carrier, trailer number, and arrival time.
S029: Yard Gate Controller is also known as Velvetrook.
S030: Drivers follow the gate instructions to the designated staging lane while a receiving door is prepared.
S031: The gate process flags unscheduled arrivals for review before they enter the receiving area.
S032: The Inbound Inspection Desk is also known as Cinderbay.
S033: The Inbound Inspection Desk checks delivery paperwork against the expected shipment and confirms the trailer is presented for inspection.
S034: Staff verify trailer identification and inspect accessible seals before unloading is authorized.
S035: Visible damage, mismatched identifiers, or compromised seals are recorded with the affected shipment details.
S036: The Inbound Inspection Desk sends the Trailer Seal Exception Note when a seal discrepancy requires follow-up.
S037: A receiving door is assigned only when the door, staging lane, and unloading crew are available.
S038: Door assignments are coordinated with the current yard position so that trailers do not obstruct active traffic routes.
S039: The Yard Gate Controller directs each cleared trailer from staging to its assigned receiving door.
S040: If a door becomes unavailable, the trailer remains in a safe holding position until a revised assignment is confirmed.
S041: The Warehouse Management System maintains the expected inbound shipment data used during receiving checks.
S042: The Warehouse Management System sends the Dispatch Wave Amendment when outbound planning requires a change.
S043: Receiving staff compare the physical pallet count with the shipment paperwork before unloading is completed.
S044: Pallets with visible damage are kept separate from acceptable stock while the discrepancy is assessed.
S045: The Inbound Inspection Desk records inspection results promptly so warehouse inventory remains aligned with the received goods.
S046: Door occupancy and clearance are monitored throughout unloading to prevent conflicting vehicle movements.
S047: Yard personnel notify receiving staff when a trailer is ready to leave the door and return to the yard route.
S048: Unloading is paused if an unsafe condition, documentation conflict, or equipment issue is discovered.
S049: The Warehouse Operations Supervisor resolves receiving issues that exceed the desk's routine authority.
S050: The receiving process closes after the shipment count, inspection status, and door release are recorded.
S051: Storage allocation begins after the shipment count, inspection status, and door release have been recorded.
S052: The Warehouse Management System evaluates available positions against pallet dimensions, mass, storage compatibility, and expected retrieval demand.
